name: Teck Resources Limited

profile.description: Teck Resources Limited is a Canadian mining company focused on copper and zinc after selling its steelmaking coal business (Elk Valley Resources) to Glencore in 2024. Core assets include the Quebrada Blanca (QB2) copper mine in Chile, Highland Valley Copper in British Columbia, the Antamina joint venture in Peru, the Red Dog zinc mine in Alaska, and the Trail metallurgical operations. Teck and Anglo American agreed in September 2025 to a merger of equals that would form Anglo Teck; shareholders approved the deal in December 2025 and closing awaits remaining regulatory approvals, including China and South Korea.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Teck has largely remade itself in five years. It sold its Elk Valley steelmaking coal business to Glencore and ramped QB2 into a large copper operation, and Q2 2026 revenue reached C$3.6B versus C$2.0B a year earlier [1][9]. AI Deployment (1/2): Teck's long-running digital program covers heads-up display technology for shovel operators and an employee idea-sharing culture launched in 2018 [7]. However, it reports no quantified AI-driven savings or revenue. Market Share (1/2): Teck is a meaningful mid-tier copper producer and a major zinc producer, but it is not a category leader and cannot set prices. Pipeline (1/2): The August 2025 operations review deferred major growth projects [6], so near-term visibility rests on QB2 optimization and the roughly US$800M of annual synergies expected from the Anglo Teck combination [1]. R&D Intensity (0/1): Reported R&D fell to C$35M in 2025 from C$157M in 2022, about 0.3% of revenue [13].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Teck's purpose, to provide essential resources the world needs to improve quality of life, is clear and ties copper and zinc to electrification. It is not distinctive among diversified miners, and the pending absorption into Anglo Teck makes its long-term continuity uncertain [1]. Community Impact (1/2): Teck has a reputation for ESG transparency and long-running health and safety commitments, and some observers call it an ESG leader in mining [9][5]. The searches did not surface specific dollar figures for community investment. Employee Retention (0/2): No turnover or tenure data was found. The 2025 operations review brought leadership changes [6], and Glassdoor reviewers cite disorganized management and weak career progression [8]. Insider Buying (0/2): The research found no meaningful net insider buying in the last 12 months.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Scored mechanically as a Growth stock [13]. Debt-to-equity of 32.4% scores 1.0, and profit margin of 25.2% scores 1.0, helped by higher copper prices and by-product credits [3]. YoY revenue growth of 33.4% scores 1.0, and forward P/E of 15.9 scores 1.0. ROE of 13.6% scores 0.91 at 2x weight. Forward PEG of 2.85 scores only 0.08 at 2x weight because analysts expect forward EPS (~$4.01) to fall below trailing EPS ($5.58) as copper prices normalize [13]. Five-year revenue CAGR is excluded as not comparable, because the 2024 coal divestiture restated history to continuing operations. Weighted sum 5.96 / 8.0 = 7.45, which rounds to 7. Liquidity floor cleared at about $182M of daily dollar volume (2.86M shares x $63.72).

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (9/9): Teck mines, concentrates and smelts copper and zinc. AI cannot substitute for this physical, permit-constrained activity, and the research found no analyst commentary that treats AI as a threat to Teck's earnings [2][4]. Copper is also a core input for AI data centers, power grids and electrification, so AI-driven capex adds to demand for Teck's main product. AI Opportunity (0/1): Teck reports no quantifiable revenue from AI products or services. Any AI tailwind reaches it indirectly through copper prices, so the tiebreaker point is not awarded.

infinite_game.summary: Teck has shown real existential flexibility by giving up a highly profitable coal franchise to become a pure-play energy-transition metals company [9]. That is the kind of pivot Sinek praises. But the company is now merging into Anglo Teck, its purpose statement is generic, and the 2025 operations review signals execution strain rather than a lived Just Cause [6]. The result is a mixed profile: courageous portfolio decisions, but an uncertain future as an independent company.

just_cause.analysis: (1/3) Teck's purpose of providing essential resources to improve quality of life is sincere but shared by nearly every miner. Its identity has changed three times in three years (coal split, coal sale, Anglo merger), so no single cause has been tested across a leadership era [1][9].

trusting_teams.analysis: (1/2) Glassdoor shows a 3.9/5 rating with 70% of employees recommending Teck, and health and safety are deeply embedded in the culture [8][5]. The 2025 operations review and leadership changes, plus reviewer complaints about disorganized management, keep this at adequate rather than high trust [6][8].

worthy_rivals.analysis: (0/1) Teck's competitive history centers on defending itself against Glencore's unsolicited 2023 bid and then negotiating a merger of equals with Anglo American [10][1]. There is little public evidence of management studying rivals to improve rather than transacting with them.

existential_flexibility.analysis: (2/2) Selling the Elk Valley steelmaking coal business, historically Teck's largest profit engine, to concentrate on copper and zinc was a transformative pivot [9][10]. Copper-driven Q2 2026 EBITDA of C$2.2B, triple the prior year, shows the pivot is working [1].

courage_to_lead.analysis: (1/2) Walking away from coal cash flows and funding QB2 through the cycle were costly long-term bets. However, deferring growth projects in the 2025 operations review [6] and agreeing to merge rather than build independently suggest a more defensive posture.

investment_thesis: Teck is now a copper-and-zinc business with real operating leverage to copper. Q2 2026 revenue rose to C$3.6B from C$2.0B, adjusted EBITDA rose 204% to C$2.2B, and adjusted EPS reached $1.93 versus $0.38 a year earlier [1][4]. The balance sheet is conservative, with debt-to-equity of 32% and about C$6.7B of cash [13]. The trailing P/E of 11.4 understates earnings power if copper stays tight. The Anglo Teck merger targets about US$800M of annual pre-tax synergies and would combine QB2 with Anglo's Collahuasi next door in Chile [1].
thesis_continued: The bear case starts with the commodity cycle. Consensus forward EPS of about $4.01 is roughly 28% below trailing EPS of $5.58, which gives a forward PEG of 2.85 [13]. Teck shareholders are also tied to a merger awaiting Chinese and South Korean approval, which leaves deal-timing and integration risk and could dilute Teck's culture inside a larger, more bureaucratic Anglo Teck [1]. Operational execution at QB2 has needed a formal operations review [6], and R&D has fallen to about 0.3% of revenue.
key_catalysts: Closing of the Anglo Teck merger after Chinese and South Korean approval, unlocking about US$800M of annual pre-tax synergies including QB2-Collahuasi integration [1]
Continued QB2 throughput and recovery improvements lifting copper volumes toward the top of guidance [1]
Structural copper deficit from AI data centers, grid upgrades and EVs supporting high copper prices and by-product credits [3]
key_risks: Copper price normalization: consensus already expects forward EPS about 28% below trailing levels [13]
Regulatory delay or added conditions on the Anglo Teck merger from China's SAMR, and integration risk after closing [1]
Operating and environmental incidents at the Chilean and Peruvian assets, such as the reported Andacollo environmental fine, plus tailings and water-permitting exposure [12]
